rubric.evidence: Every claim traces to a primary source fetched live on 2026-07-26: the merged FedID Digital Credentials draft carries the full surface in normative sections (DigitalCredentialGetRequest/CreateRequest with required DOMString protocol; the presentation enum — openid4vp-v1-unsigned/-signed/-multisigned, org-iso-mdoc; the issuance enum — openid4vci-v1; DigitalCredential.protocol echoing the protocol used; userAgentAllowsProtocol() with the exact contract: unknown identifier returns false without throwing, undefined interface throws ReferenceError, typeof guard required). The 151-developer-trial/160-removal timeline comes from the ChromeStatus API record; the flag DigitalCredentialsProtocolFilter (experimental) from runtime_enabled_features.json5. The substantive MDN check: API/DigitalCredential and the userAgentAllowsProtocol_static subpage both 404.

Feature id 6492906882990080 appears in the v151 milestone listing under 'In developer trial (Behind a flag)'; route slug derives from the listing name per the documented slug rule; H1 is the listing name verbatim; the warn-block names the exact flag.

Exact 3-item inventory: the static userAgentAllowsProtocol() method, the protocol member (required on both request dictionaries + echoed on the credential), and the two protocol enumerations (mapped to the protocol-member page covering them). Overview links both stable routes; each child covers all nine dimensions. reference-contract.json maps 11 sources, 27 dimension coverages; deliberately partial pending independent review.

The overview separates the deprecation story (unspecified protocols phasing out, 151 trial → 160 removal) from the durable pattern (explicit protocol + userAgentAllowsProtocol() gate). The error contract is presented exactly: false-on-unknown is a feature (forward-compat probe), ReferenceError-on-undefined is the trap (typeof guard first).

Overview embeds the identity-verified showcase protocol-allowlist (200, same chromestatus id) with a linked source label; snippets follow the spec's own two-step gate pattern (typeof check → protocol check) and a compliant request shape.

Real BCD-backed rows (protocol, userAgentAllowsProtocol_static, data: Chrome 141, Safari 26, Edge mirror, FF false) kept strictly separate from the ChromeStatus-sourced 151-trial/160-removal timeline — the tables say so explicitly. Vendor signals from the ChromeStatus API record (FF No signal, Safari Shipped, web-devs No signals).

Direct primary-source link contract: the FedID protocols section and the specific dom- anchors (getrequest, presentation/issuance enums, credential protocol, userAgentAllowsProtocol — all verified resolvable), runtime_enabled_features.json5, ChromeStatus page + API record, BCD file, issue #396, and the three showcase routes — each named source separately linked, target=_blank rel=noopener, zero plain-text labels.

Single main and h1 per page; sequential h1→h2; tables with captions and scoped headers; banner role=note with aria-label; warn-block for the flag-gated trial; descriptive iframe title; <wbr> hints in long H1s.

First-column width hints and compat-table column min-widths applied from the start (cycle-8/9/10 lessons); MCP matrix at 1280x800 and 390x844 verifies no document overflow on all three routes; pre blocks scroll internally by design.

Iframe src is the feature's own stable showcase route (protocol-allowlist), identity-matched to chromestatus id 6492906882990080 and HEAD-verified 200 alongside the compliant-request-builder and deprecation-migration siblings (linked in See also). cpsFeature.conformanceRoute is the feature-level route (corrected from the generated concept route before commit). No repointing, no forked platform assertions.
